title: Unpaired Multi-Modal Segmentation via Knowledge Distillation
mechanism: Segment two unpaired modalities with fully shared conv kernels, modality-specific normalisation layers and a KL loss aligning per-class prediction distributions across modalities.
adaptation: Joint training of our EL cells with crack-labelled UVF cells (OpenUVF, 3000 labelled cells) and optionally UCF-EL as a second EL modality; crack + background only for the extra modality; own BN per modality; keeps the extra knowledge in shared weights instead of a pretrain that the fine-tune erases.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + joint OpenUVF batches with own BN and KL prototype loss; baseline: PF. Metrics: CV crack relF1@2 and E1 crack recall. Kill if both < +0.01. Download needs user OK.
evidence: R: cardiac and abdominal CT/MRI unpaired segmentation beats single-modality and naive joint training (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: Partial: UCF-EL encoder pretraining then house fine-tune was n.d. (encoder erased). Joint multi-dataset / cross-modality training is untested.
